title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: parent-level permissions for ServiceNow and Confluence
summary: Hold: the licensing paragraph incorrectly implies that synced connector grounding does not require the Copilot entitlement shown in Microsoft's licensing table. Jira is also present in the roadmap description, not just its title. The permission risks and the reported disagreement about Confluence parent permissions are otherwise supported.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The July 15, 2026 release-note entry for this feature names Confluence and ServiceNow, not Jira.
claims.quote:
## July 15, 2026
Admins can manage access more precisely with support for nested permissions in Confluence and ServiceNow

claims.where: summary; What's changing: first and third paragraphs
claims.claim: The release note says Confluence now evaluates parent-level permissions for child items, while the briefing also reports the conflicting setup documentation.
claims.quote: The connectors for Confluence and ServiceNow now evaluate parent-level permissions when determining access to child items.

claims.where: summary; What's changing: ServiceNow paragraph; rationale: risk
claims.claim: ServiceNow Knowledge hierarchical permissions evaluate knowledge base parent permissions together with article child permissions.
claims.quote: ServiceNow Knowledge supports setting permissions at both the knowledge base (parent) level and the individual article (child) level. The system evaluates these permissions together to determine whether a user has access to an article.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph
claims.claim: Previously the Confluence and ServiceNow connectors considered only child item permissions.
claims.quote: Previously, only child item permissions were considered, which could lead to inconsistent access control.

claims.where: Why it matters: first paragraph
claims.claim: Microsoft describes the earlier permission evaluation as capable of inconsistent access control.
claims.quote: Previously, only child item permissions were considered, which could lead to inconsistent access control.

claims.where: What's changing: ServiceNow paragraph
claims.claim: The July 1, 2026 release note says admins previously had to create new ServiceNow Knowledge and Catalog connections to adopt hierarchical permissions.
claims.quote: Previously, admins had to create new connections to adopt hierarchical permissions for ServiceNow Knowledge and Catalog Copilot Connectors because editing was not supported.

claims.where: What's changing: ServiceNow paragraph; Governance controls: closing prose
claims.claim: The July 1, 2026 release note for roadmap item 505438 says existing ServiceNow Knowledge and Catalog connections can switch between Simple and Advanced handling.
claims.quote: Now, admins can easily edit their existing connections to switch between the permission handling option i.e. Simple vs Advanced to quickly adopt to the hierarchical permission feature.

claims.where: What's changing: Confluence paragraph; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The Confluence Cloud setup page says parent page permissions are not considered, conflicting with the release note.
claims.quote: Permissions are managed only at the space and page level. Parent page permissions aren't considered.

claims.where: What's changing: Confluence paragraph
claims.claim: The Confluence setup page describes synced nested groups as usable for ACLs, separately from parent-page permissions.
claims.quote: You can use synced nested groups to manage access control lists (ACLs), provided the nested group's members are part of a Confluence user group.
claims.fix: Append 'provided the nested group's members are part of a Confluence user group' to the sentence describing synced nested groups.

claims.where: What's changing: Jira paragraph
claims.claim: Jira Cloud connector documentation describes project permission schemes and issue-level security.
claims.quote: In Atlassian Jira, security permissions are defined using project permission schemes containing site-level groups and project roles. Issue-level security can also be defined using issue-level permission schemes.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/jira-cloud-deployment to sources; it states the project permission-scheme fact.

claims.where: What's changing: Jira paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The Jira Cloud connector pages checked do not document hierarchical or nested permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: "Jira Cloud" "permission schemes" "nested"; read jira-cloud-overview and the jira-cloud-deployment and jira-cloud-admin-setup search excerpts. Found project schemes and issue-level security, not hierarchical or nested permissions.

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors hierarchical parent permissions existing connections automatic default ServiceNow Confluence; read roadmap, July release notes, ServiceNow setup/deployment and Confluence setup/overview. No explicit automatic adoption statement found.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Simple is the default ServiceNow Knowledge user-criteria flow.
claims.quote: The ServiceNow Knowledge connector supports two flows for user criteria permissions: Simple (default) and Advanced.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: ServiceNow Simple flow does not evaluate advanced script-based user criteria.
claims.quote: The default is Simple. In this flow, advanced script-based user criteria aren't evaluated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Simple flow skips an advanced script-based Can Read criterion, which can cause oversharing.
claims.quote: If an advanced script-based user criterion exists on the Can Read (allow) path of a knowledge base or article, the Simple flow can't evaluate the script to determine which users are allowed, so it skips that user criterion, which might result in oversharing.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Simple flow treats an advanced script-based Cannot Read criterion as deny all, blocking the affected content for all users.
claims.quote: the connector conservatively treats the criterion as deny all, so the affected knowledge base or article content is blocked for all users in Copilot and search results.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Advanced flow evaluates script-based criteria by calling a Scripted REST API that must be set up in ServiceNow.
claims.quote: This flow evaluates script-based user criteria by calling the Scripted REST API in ServiceNow, which ensures accurate permissions handling when content is ingested into Microsoft Graph. For the Advanced option to work properly, you need to Set up REST API.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Without read access to sys_properties, the ServiceNow connector defaults to the most restrictive property settings.
claims.quote: If the service account can't read these properties, the connector silently defaults to the most restrictive settings (true for both)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: That restrictive fallback blocks articles without explicit user criteria from search results.
claims.quote: which blocks articles without explicit user criteria from appearing in search results.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: For HR Service Delivery knowledge bases in sn_hr_core scope, the service account needs sn_hr_core.content_reader or sn_hr_core.admin to read the scoped user criteria.
claims.quote: verify that the service account has the sn_hr_core.content_reader or sn_hr_core.admin role. Without one of these roles, the service account can't read HR-scoped user criteria.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Missing an HR-scoped role can cause HR-restricted articles to be indexed as accessible to all users.
claims.quote: Because the connector receives empty results rather than an error, it might interpret HR-restricted articles as having no access restrictions and index them as accessible to all users.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Visible to everyone makes indexed connector content accessible to all users in the organisation instead of enforcing source ACLs.
claims.quote:
Only people with access to this data source: The connector respects source system access control lists (ACLs).
Visible to everyone: The connector grants access to all users in the organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Confluence connector identity mapping matches Confluence email addresses to Microsoft Entra ID user principal names.
claims.quote: The connector maps Confluence user accounts to Microsoft 365 (Entra ID) identities. If Confluence users' emails match their Entra ID UPNs, this mapping is automatic.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: When those identities differ, a mapping must be configured or some content might not appear for intended users.
claims.quote: Without this mapping, some content might not appear for intended users because the service can't verify that they have access.
claims.fix: Replace the identity-mapping risk bullet with 'The Confluence overview says email-to-UPN mismatches require manual mapping and can hide intended content. The setup page instead describes default matching against either the Entra ID UPN or email address; check both before configuring a mapping.' Both https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/confluence-cloud-overview and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/confluence-cloud-admin-setup are already cited.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: ServiceNow incremental crawls do not update article permissions when knowledge-base parent permissions change.
claims.quote: Doesn't update user-to-criteria mappings (identity sync) or permissions for articles where knowledge base (parent) level permissions changed.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Confluence permission changes are picked up only by full crawls, not incremental syncs.
claims.quote: Permission changes are picked up only during a full crawl (once every 24 hours by default), not during the 15-minute incremental syncs.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The default Confluence full-crawl interval is 24 hours.
claims.quote: once every 24 hours by default
